- De Morgan's law for unions states that $$\overline{A \cup B} \equiv \overline{A} \cap \overline{B}.$$
- De Morgan's law for intersections states that $$\overline{A \cap B} \equiv \overline{A} \cup \overline{B}.$$

Intuitively, you can think that the complement "flips" the union into an intersection and vice versa.

To demonstrate De Morgan's laws, consider the sets $A = \{ 1,2,3 \}$ and $B = \{ 3,4 \}$ in the universe $U = \{ 1,2,3,4,5,6 \}.$

- Computing $\overline{A \cap B},$ we have $$\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A\cap B} & =\overset{―}{{1,2,3}\cap {3,4}} \\ & =\overset{―}{{3}} \\ & ={1,2,4,5,6}.\end{aligned}$$ Computing $\overline{A} \cup \overline{B},$ we have $$\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A}\cup \overset{―}{B} & =\overset{―}{{1,2,3}}\cup \overset{―}{{3,4}} \\ & ={4,5,6}\cup {1,2,5,6} \\ & ={1,2,4,5,6}.\end{aligned}$$ So, we have that $\overline{A \cap B} = \overline{A} \cup \overline{B}. \quad \color{green}\checkmark$" :tutorial/id #uuid "df8a49e7-15bf-53b1-9af3-754dbf9fc0e8" :tutorial/math-academy-id 4366 :tutorial/title "Introduction"} :step/id #uuid "1f2c991b-1f17-5ca9-b2bb-adab88ae5d59" :step/math-academy-id 26659 :step/next {:db/id 17592186153139}} {:db/id 17592186153139 :step/content {:db/id 17592186153402 :tutorial/content "For the sets $A = \{ 1,2,3 \}$ and $B = \{ 3,4 \}$ in the universe $U = \{ 1,2,3,4,5,6 \},$ the region $\overline{A \cup B} = \overline{A} \cap \overline{B}$ is shown below:

A robust knowledge of set theory is another cornerstone of mathematical proof-writing. By the end of the course, students will appreciate how set theory provides a comprehensive toolkit for proving mathematical results.
After mastering these fundamentals, students will explore various proof-writing techniques, including direct proof, proof by cases, proof by contrapositive, proof by contradiction, disproof, and mathematical induction. The course emphasizes proving concepts related to parity, divisibility, congruence, sequences, functions, set identities, and relations. Students will have multiple opportunities to test and refine their proof construction and comprehension skills throughout the course and in varied contexts

complement of a union or intersection.

- De Morgan's law for unions states that $$\overline{A \cup B} \equiv \overline{A} \cap \overline{B}.$$
- De Morgan's law for intersections states that $$\overline{A \cap B} \equiv \overline{A} \cup \overline{B}.$$

Intuitively, you can think that the complement "flips" the union into an intersection and vice versa.

To demonstrate De Morgan's laws, consider the sets $A = \{ 1,2,3 \}$ and $B = \{ 3,4 \}$ in the universe $U = \{ 1,2,3,4,5,6 \}.$

- Computing $\overline{A \cup B},$ we have $$\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A\cup B} & =\overset{―}{{1,2,3}\cup {3,4}} \\ & =\overset{―}{{1,2,3,4}} \\ & ={5,6}.\end{aligned}$$ Computing $\overline{A} \cap \overline{B},$ we have $$\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A}\cap \overset{―}{B} & =\overset{―}{{1,2,3}}\cap \overset{―}{{3,4}} \\ & ={4,5,6}\cap {1,2,5,6} \\ & ={5,6}.\end{aligned}$$ So, we have that $\overline{A \cup B} = \overline{A} \cap \overline{B}. \quad \color{green}\checkmark$
- Computing $\overline{A \cap B},$ we have $$\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A\cap B} & =\overset{―}{{1,2,3}\cap {3,4}} \\ & =\overset{―}{{3}} \\ & ={1,2,4,5,6}.\end{aligned}$$ Computing $\overline{A} \cup \overline{B},$ we have $$\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A}\cup \overset{―}{B} & =\overset{―}{{1,2,3}}\cup \overset{―}{{3,4}} \\ & ={4,5,6}\cup {1,2,5,6} \\ & ={1,2,4,5,6}.\end{aligned}$$ So, we have that $\overline{A \cap B} = \overline{A} \cup \overline{B}. \quad \color{green}\checkmark$" 17592186045585] [17592186153401 1065 4366 17592186045585] [17592186153401 1066 #uuid "df8a49e7-15bf-53b1-9af3-754dbf9fc0e8" 17592186045585] [17592186153401 1067 "Introduction" 17592186045585] [17592186153402 1064 "For the sets $A = \{ 1,2,3 \}$ and $B = \{ 3,4 \}$ in the universe $U = \{ 1,2,3,4,5,6 \},$ the region $\overline{A \cup B} = \overline{A} \cap \overline{B}$ is shown below:
